harnesses.label: Codex CLI
harnesses.note: Codex updates preserve a proven installed source: Homebrew uses brew upgrade, npm installs the checked stable version only when the selected executable belongs to @openai/codex, and the official standalone package uses codex update. Standalone checks read the published npm version without invoking the updater; an unconfirmed stable release or unknown shim refuses the update.

harnesses.label: Claude Code
harnesses.note: Claude Code's stable channel: the check reads the release npm tags stable, without touching the installation, and an upgrade installs exactly that release with Claude Code's own installer (claude install <version>).

harnesses.label: Hermes Agent
harnesses.note: Only published stable Hermes releases are offered. The check reads the official GitHub release without fetching a development branch; Upgrade uses Hermes's transient stable channel and keeps its backup. Older Hermes versions that do not support --channel refuse the update rather than falling back to main.

harnesses.label: Oh My Pi
harnesses.note: Oh My Pi's release is read from its npm package without touching the installation, and "omp update" installs it the way omp was installed (Bun or its standalone binary).

harnesses.label: Cline
harnesses.note: The Cline CLI from npm. It is updated where it is installed: npm global, Homebrew, or an npm folder of its own (npm install --prefix). Its own updater may install elsewhere, so an unproven source is refused.

harnesses.label: Kilo Code
harnesses.note: The Kilo Code CLI from npm. It is updated where it is installed: npm global, Homebrew, or an npm folder of its own (npm install --prefix). Its own updater may install elsewhere, so an unproven source is refused.

harnesses.label: Grok Build
harnesses.note: Grok Build's own updater checks without installing (update --check --json) and installs the stable channel's newest build. Stepsemble starts Grok with --no-auto-update, so it is updated here or in Grok itself.
